## Changes
- **Esc steps back one point while drawing.** Esc now removes the last point placed, as Backspace does. A stray Esc no longer throws away every point of a building, barrier, road or outline in progress.
  - Shift+Esc clears the whole shape.
  - With no points left, Esc returns to Select as before.
  - The sheet's outline tool works the same way.
- **The Sheet view keeps up with the drawing.** On very fine grids the sheet waited about 1.5 s after a new drawing was ready before showing it. It now shows it within about a tenth of a second (P2012 at 0.125 m, 447,000 points).
- **No pauses when the sheet refreshes on Retina screens.** The sheet is now drawn in several short steps, so the window is never held for more than about 35 ms. The result is still identical, pixel for pixel, to the exported sheet.

## Changes
- **Contours draw the same however the model sits.** A map now draws identically when the model is moved to national-grid coordinates, turned or mirrored. Five orientation-dependent steps in the drawing were fixed, so lines and bands may move slightly on some maps, typically a fraction of a square metre per band.
  - **Wrong levels on some lines:** a contour line lying wholly inside a building or a no-data area dropped its line but not its level, so the lines after it carried the wrong level (a 50 dB line could be drawn as 45).
  - **Thin slivers:** these took their band from a point chosen in an orientation-dependent way.
  - **Shadow edges:** two cases in finding them depended on the frame.
- **Long curves stay curved at high Smoothing.** At linked 75–100 %, long outer contours no longer flatten into straight chords. Simplify at 100 % with Smoothing off is unchanged.
- **Cancelling a drawing takes effect at once,** within a twentieth of a second, even on very dense maps.
- **The first contour drawing after installing is quick.** Every drawing kernel is now prepared when the app is built, not on your Mac.
- **Contour calculations keep to their time limit.** A calculation given a time limit now stops on time and releases its workers; before, a large grid could run on for minutes.
- **Calculation workers no longer grow in memory.** Caches that were almost never reused grew by about 3 MB per receiver; on a 2,200-receiver grid each worker now stays near 540 MB instead of growing to 1.9 GB. Results and speed are unchanged.
- **The old contour code has been removed.** About 65,000 lines of the previous drawing and hidden-refinement code are gone; nothing used them any more. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Known limitations:**
  - **Speed on the busiest maps:** shaped contours on the busiest maps (for example 32,000 points with many bands) take about 1.2 s to draw; a faster shape stage follows in 0.86.1.
  - **Sheet view on very fine grids:** the Sheet view can take a few seconds to show a new shape on very fine grids (0.125 m and finer).

## Bug fixes
- **Validation presets open with their own receptor IDs again.** 0.85.1 renumbered the receptors of the built-in, read-only validation projects when they were opened. Read-only projects are no longer changed on open.
- **Bands no longer cross inside other bands at Simplify 100 %.** A rare case could leave neighbouring bands overlapping where a simplified line dragged a collapsed neighbour with it.

## Changes
- **Every Simplify and Smoothing setting now looks right.**
  - **Linked settings:** moving the linked control from 0 to 100 % now goes evenly from accurate contours to fluid curves. Linked 50 % is no longer more angular than either end: a single awkward line used to make the whole drawing fall back to its simplified, straight-edged form.
  - **Smoothing and Simplify together:** Smoothing keeps pace with Simplify, so any corner Simplify makes is rounded whenever Smoothing is on.
  - **Simplify alone:** Simplify at 100 % with Smoothing off stays plainly geometric.
- **Shadow edges stay straight and in place.** Where buildings or barriers start to screen a source, the level really does step, so that line never bends or moves. Where contours meet it, the corners round off more as Smoothing rises.
- **The Objects key names things the way you would.**
  - **One object:** a single point source, line source, area source, receptor, road, railway, barrier or parking lot shows its own name, for example "Air Source Heat Pump", or else the singular "Point Source".
  - **Several objects:** they show a name they share ("ASHP" for ASHP 1 and ASHP 2), or else the plural with a count ("Point Sources (3)").
  - **Generated names:** IDs such as SRC_001 are never shown as names.

## Bug fixes
- **Receptor IDs stay in step with their numbers.** Turning off a receptor stack left a gap in the IDs: on P2012, receptors numbered 1 and 2 on the plan were REC_001 and REC_003 in results. Turning a stack off now renumbers like any delete, and a project saved with gaps opens with consecutive IDs.
  - Default-style names follow the new IDs; names you gave your receptors stay.
  - Per-receptor inputs move with their receptor.
  - Results are recalculated after the IDs change.
- **Contour bands no longer reach inside buildings at shaped settings.** Simplify could cut a corner across a building, so neighbouring bands overlapped inside it (P1949, P1986, P2001). The building hid this on screen, but it reached GIS exports.
- **A window-styling error no longer appears in the error log.** AURIS checks the windows' native styling every tenth of a second, and it could stop on an object that was not a window.

## New features
- **Noise maps are drawn by a new engine, built from the ground up.** Calculate now solves the grid and nothing else. Drawing the map is a separate, fast step that never calculates, and it runs in the background so the window never waits:
  - **The calculated grid shows straight away.** The contours follow, typically within a second.
  - **Shape changes redraw quickly.** Simplify and Smoothing take about half a second or less.
  - **View-only changes repaint at once.** Colours, opacity, lines, labels and blend start no job.
  - **Drawing never stalls.** Switching style or cancelling never leaves the map blank: the last drawing stays until the new one arrives. On P2012 (0.5 m grid) switching to smoothed contours used to sit at 97 % for minutes while it made hidden extra calculations. It now draws in under a second.
- **Contours are smooth at any grid spacing, with sharp shadow edges.**
  - **Interpolation.** Bands and lines are drawn from one interpolated field that never overshoots the calculated levels.
  - **Walls and holes.** A level is never interpolated through a wall, and buildings are exact holes. There is no staircase, and no white gaps round buildings on coarse grids.
  - **Shadow edges.** Behind buildings and barriers they are found from the geometry, kept only where the calculated grid shows the step, and drawn as clean straight wedges.
  - **Accuracy.** Measured against exact solves at 0.125 m, the drawing is two to four times closer to the true field than plain interpolation. On P2012 the 95th-percentile error is 0.03 dB on a 0.5 m grid.
- **Simplify and Smoothing apply to every band boundary.**
  - **Simplify** makes them geometric, with straight runs and corners; at 100 % it is plainly geometric.
  - **Smoothing** then turns them into curves.
  - **Linked or separate.** The two controls are linked by default and can be split.
  - **Scale-free.** They behave the same on a 50 m site and a 5 km map.
  - **Bounded.** At 100 % a line may move until the field under it differs by half a band step; walls and the map edge never move.
  - **Receptors stay in their band.** Every receptor stays in the band of its own level at every setting.
- **SVG and PDF exports carry true curves.** Smoothed contours are written as cubic Bézier curves, so they edit cleanly in drawing software. Each boundary is fitted once, so neighbouring bands cannot gap. DXF, GeoPackage and GeoJSON keep dense polylines, which every CAD and GIS package reads reliably.
- **dB labels follow the lines.** Labels sit on straight-enough stretches of each line, upright and with a halo, and the line is cut beneath each label. They avoid each other, receptor names and the legend, and stay put when you pan.
- **One drawing everywhere.** The plan view, Sheet, PNG, PDF and SVG exports, GIS export, the 3D view, section views, the cursor readout and the receptor check all use the same drawing, so an export always matches the screen.
- **A drawing that cannot be made never takes the app with it.** If a drawing fails, runs over its time or memory budget, or its worker crashes:
  - the calculated grid stays on screen with a note in the panel: "Contours couldn't be drawn for this map. Showing the calculated grid. Details saved.";
  - the worker restarts;
  - the inputs are saved to a small file, and "Show details" opens it, so the problem can be reproduced exactly.

## Changes
- **The Contours panel is reorganised.**
  - **Result page:** Grid spacing, Receiver height and Calculation margin now sit together under Calculation. Changing one marks the result out of date in place.
  - **Contours page:** Colours, Drawing (*Calculated grid* or *Contours*, with Simplify and Smoothing), Lines and labels, and Fill. Lines and labels are shown for both styles.
  - **Labelled buttons:** Normalise, Save palette… and Reset are labelled buttons.
  - **Progress:** the footer shows the drawing's real progress, for example "Drawing contours… 45 %".
- **Interpolated Raster, Acoustic Scalar Field, Detail and Preset are gone.**
  - Contours at Simplify 0 and Smoothing 0 is the interpolated field, and Gradient is the smooth colour field.
  - Detail is chosen automatically.
  - Settings › Solver oversampling and the unused default-band settings are removed.
- **Existing sheets convert when opened.**
  - SmartSmooth keeps its Simplify and Smoothing values.
  - Raw becomes Calculated grid.
  - Interpolated Raster and Scalar Field become Contours at 0 / 0, or Gradient where they were drawn as a gradient.
  - Calculated grids are kept; old cached drawings are redrawn.
- **Calculated levels are unchanged.** Only the drawing is new.
- **Known limitations in this release:**
  - **Shape at 50 %:** Simplify and Smoothing at about 50 % linked draw more angular than intended; Off and 100 % look right. A fix follows in 0.85.1.
  - **Band edges inside buildings:** at shaped settings, neighbouring bands can overlap by a fraction of a square metre inside building footprints. On screen and in image exports the building covers it; GIS exports carry it. A fix follows in 0.85.1.
  - **First drawing after installing:** the first contour drawing takes a few seconds while its kernels are prepared; after that it is quick.
  - **Close to walls and sources:** within one grid cell of a wall or a source the map is only as fine as the grid, as with any contour map; use a finer grid there.
  - **Many narrow bands:** shape changes with very many narrow bands (for example 60 bands of 1 dB) can take over a second.
  - **3D bands:** in the 3D view, Contours in Bands is drawn as a flat texture without relief shading; Calculated grid and Gradient keep it.
  - **Dark mode:** the plan canvas does not follow dark mode (unchanged).
- **Faster terrain screening.** The terrain profile walk no longer repeats itself from the receiver end, and starts from the triangulation's cell index. Contours on scattered-terrain models are about 4 % faster, with identical results.

## Bug fixes
- **Switching back to the calculated grid no longer leaves the footer at "Finalising noise map… 0 %".** Leaving Raw had started a hidden calculation that switching back did not cancel.
- **"LAFmax events on sheet" is now saved with the project.** It was dropped on save and reopen.
- **Contour lines no longer appear where no band edge exists.** Some saved maps drew lines along shadow edges or the map edge with no band change across them.

## Changes
- **Rectangular buildings and barriers no longer slow the whole calculation.** A building or barrier drawn as a rectangle square to the grid was handed to the calculation as a different kind of object, which the fast compiled engine could not take. One such object sent every source–receiver pair in the model to the slower reference engine: 4 to 6 times slower. They are now calculated like any other footprint, with identical results to the bit. P1949, P1963 and P2000 each had one.
- **Contours of area sources and car parks are faster.** Each plain section of an area source (no directivity, no attenuation area) is now handed to the calculation without the per-section bookkeeping it never needed. Results are identical to the bit. CPU time for a 4 m grid falls by 11% for large area sources and 7% for car parks.
- **Façade and break-out sources use the reference engine again.** 0.83 moved sources radiating from a wall onto the compiled engine. Where break-out panes meet at a building's corner, that engine counted some routes that leave through the wall itself, which the reference engine correctly stops. Single routes differed by up to 22 dB; contour levels by at most 0.003 dB, and receptor levels not at all, on every model checked. No real project changed: P1922 and every padel project give the same receptor levels, padel LAFmax results and contours either way. Contours of models with wall sources take the same time as in 0.83 or less.

## Bug fixes
- **A screening building's drawing direction no longer changes a level.** Over a building whose roof gives two parallel edges, ISO 9613-2's route (7.4.2) was built along the direction the building's walls were drawn in. For a building drawn clockwise its points came out receiver first. A façade pane, a break-out source or a directional source behind it then took its radiation correction toward a point behind itself, as if radiating through its own wall: up to 8 dB low. Ordinary sources were never affected, because the barrier attenuation itself is symmetric. No real project changed: P1922, P2006 and every padel project give the same receptor levels and padel LAFmax results before and after.
- **CRTN: a wall reflects only for the roads it is near.** The opposite-façade correction (CRTN paragraph 26.2) counted a wall within 100 m of any switched-on road as an opposite façade of every road. Switching one road on could raise another road's level, and a project's total was not the sum of its roads. Each road now uses only the walls within 100 m of itself. No real project changed: every project with a single switched-on road is identical, and P1987, with three roads, is unchanged.
- **CRN: far-side reflections no longer depend on which way the site faces.** The opposite-façade correction compares the track's angle of view with each far-side building's. Where the view crossed due east of the receiver, the two could be measured on different turns of the compass and miss each other, and the correction (up to about 0.5 dB) was lost. P1944, the only project with a railway, is unchanged.
- **A court's ends and sides no longer depend on the corner its outline starts at.** Every court calculation, and the plan and 3D drawing, took the first edge of the outline as the court's length. A court whose corners started on a short edge had its glass ends along its sides and its "beside the court" measurement position at an end: up to 1.7 dB. The length is now always the longer edge. Courts drawn with the court tool were never affected, and no real project changed: P1976a and P1976b each have two such courts, and their receptor levels are identical.
- **Light mode always returns to light colours.** If AURIS first switched mode while its palette was dark, light mode later kept some dark backgrounds.

## New features
- **Padel: strikes and panel impacts as two events, each from its own data.** A new LAFmax method, *Strike + panel*, treats the two things a padel court is heard for separately, as ProPG's two measurement positions do:
  - **Ball strikes.** Every in-play position on a 1 m grid. The sound power is fitted so that the 90th percentile over those positions equals the typical LAFmax measured beside the court. ProPG's typical maximum, the 10th percentile of event maxima, is the level 10 % of events exceed.
  - **The ball on the enclosure.** Every glass and mesh panel. The sound power is fitted so that the 90th percentile over the rebound wall's panels equals the typical LAFmax measured behind it.

  Each receptor takes the louder of its loudest strike and its loudest panel impact, never the two added together. The responsible position shows on the plan and in the Inspector. The loudest strike is often not the nearest: strikes beside receptor-facing glass are screened by it.

  The check shows each mechanism reproducing its own position, and what it gives alone at the other position, where the other mechanism should dominate. On the P2003 court: strikes alone give 57.4 dB behind against 62 dB measured, and panel impacts alone give 59.9 dB beside against 70 dB.

  The upper range adds each mechanism's own spread in the data: with ProPG Table 13.26, strikes +15 dB and panel impacts +13 dB.

  The method needs data at both positions; ProPG Tables 13.25 and 13.26 have them. It reproduces the P2003 audit to the second decimal: strike power 99.35 dB, and Haven Lodge first floor 52.99 dB. Courts on the existing methods are unchanged.
- **"Struck panels reflect from their own glass" is a visible setting.** Under Inspector › Padel court › Event details. Off, a struck panel's event is not mirrored by the court's own glass; that was the method before and is still the default. On is a sensitivity: on the P2003 court the panel power is refitted 2.6 dB lower, and panel levels at the receptors change by up to 2.6 dB.
- **Exports say where their numbers came from.** Results' Excel export, the compliance JSON and the padel Excel export now carry a Provenance sheet:
  - the project file and whether it was saved;
  - the calculation run and whether it still matches the model;
  - the acoustic input and calculation fingerprints.

  An export from a model with unsaved changes also saves the model as calculated beside it ("… - model as exported.ap"), so issued figures can be reproduced. Each padel court's basis now lists the LWAFmax and event height its levels actually used.
- **A supported scripting interface.** `auris.api` gives scripts a stable set of functions:
  - open a project read-only;
  - receptor levels;
  - single-event maxima at receptors;
  - the padel comparison;
  - British National Grid conversion;
  - bearings and compass words in AURIS's +y-south model frame.

  docs/scripting.md has a worked example. A script run from standard input, or without an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard, now calculates in one process with a warning, where it used to crash with BrokenProcessPool.

## Changes
- **Area sources are integrated to convergence, at receptors and contour nodes alike.** ISO 9613-2 Clause 4 only asks that each section of an area source be no larger than half its distance. AURIS used an eighth. Far from the source that still leaves sections metres across, and the ground and screening terms vary across them. Every section is now also no larger than a thirty-second of its distance, or 2 m if that is larger. Sources near the point being calculated, where sections are already small, are split as before and take no longer. On every project in the corpus, receptors are within 0.03 dB of a 1/128 reference, where they were up to 0.28 dB off. Receptors and contour nodes use the same rule, so a node still equals a receptor at its position.

  Receptor changes:

  | Project | Largest change |
  |---|---|
  | P2003 De Montfort House | −0.30 dB (−0.01 dB on average) |
  | P2005 Unit A | +0.06 dB |
  | P2001 Aberdare | +0.05 dB |
  | P1922 | −0.01 dB |
  | P2001 Rogerstone | 0.001 dB |

  Contours (4 m raw grids):
  - P2003: 95 % of nodes within 0.19 dB. At one node in deep shadow, 93 m from the court, the old level was 3.7 dB low: 16.3 against a converged 19.9 dB, which the 1/128 reference agrees on.
  - P2001 Aberdare: 95 % within 0.09 dB, at most 0.6 dB.

  Contours near area sources take a little longer: P2003's grid 4.7 s instead of 4.0 s, P2001 Aberdare's 192 s instead of 168 s. Receptor runs take about the same. Courts calibrated through the model are recalibrated once, then cached as before. The rule is a project setting, and part of the calculation fingerprint.
- **Vertical and façade sources calculate on the compiled engine.** A source radiating from a wall, such as a façade break-out pane or a vertical area source on a building, used to take the slower reference engine for every path. The compiled engine now takes it, with identical results to the bit, checked all round the host building. P1922's receptor run takes 1.6 s instead of 4–6 s. Its single-threaded contour grid takes 122 s instead of 194 s. Its parallel 4 m grid is unchanged on a loaded machine, at about 12.5 s.
- **Model checks flag a court still following sloping ground.** Courts drawn before 0.76 can still tilt with the natural slope. The check gives the fall across the court and points to Level all courts.
- **Draft contour accuracy states its vertical-source limit.** Draft doesn't refine vertical sources near the ground and their edges. Applying that refinement in Draft was measured on P1922: the error against Exact fell from p95 1.07 dB to 0.57 dB, but Draft then took 11.5 s against Exact's 13.4 s. Draft stays fast, and its description now says it can be up to about 3 dB out behind vertical sources.

## Bug fixes
- **The parking toolbar test no longer fails under parallel test runs.** It checked the sign blue in whatever mode an earlier test had left the app in; dark mode lifts that blue for contrast.
- **"ProPG" is no longer lower-cased in the padel statistic menu.**

## Changes
- **Faster exact calculations beside padel courts and other walled sources.** Cutting an area source along its screening and reflection planes can leave pieces under a micron across. When one of those pieces sat exactly on a wall corner, the compiled engine handed the pair to the slower reference engine, at about 0.3 s a pair. The compiled engine now treats the piece and the corner as one point on the route, as the reference does. Exact points on P2001 Aberdare are 18 % faster. Results are identical.

## Bug fixes
- **Vertical area sources with a reflection now calculate.** Since 0.42, a vertical area source (a façade break-out pane, or a padel panel drawn as a vertical source) stopped the calculation with an error whenever one of its paths reflected off a wall. The reflection search handed its wall openings to the vertical-source integration in a form that integration could not read. It now reads both forms. Other source types are unchanged.
- **Vertical area sources are integrated to convergence.** ISO 9613-2 splits an area source into sections no larger than k times their distance to the receiver. That keeps the path to the receiver representative, but a vertical source also spans heights close to the ground and often stands against a screening edge, such as its own wall's top or end. There, the ground and screening terms change across the source on a scale of metres or centimetres, not tens of metres. A 2 m padel panel 100 m away was treated as one section and read up to 2.7 dB low. Each section of a vertical source is now also kept no larger than half its height above the ground (down to 1 m), and half its distance to the nearest screening edge or, for a reflected path, its reflector (down to 0.25 m). On the 52 panels of a padel court, AURIS now agrees with a 3 cm point-by-point reference within 0.3 dB (95 % within 0.1 dB), where it differed by up to 2.8 dB. On P1922's 11 façade break-out panes, receptors move by 0.01 dB at most, and contour levels behind the buildings by up to 1.5 dB (95 % within 0.75 dB), towards the converged values. Contours with vertical sources take longer: P1922's 4 m raw grid takes 20 s instead of 7 s. Horizontal area sources are unchanged.
- **No more grey squares along CRTN roads on contour maps.** The CRTN method gives no level to a receiver exactly on a road's emission line. A sloping road passes exactly through a contour node now and then, and so does every road vertex placed on a whole metre. Each of those nodes was left empty, and the road surface showed through as a grey square. Each node is now drawn as the energy mean of the levels 1 mm either side of the road. The two sides differ by 0.1–0.3 dB mid-span and up to about 6 dB at the apex of a bend. A receptor placed exactly on a road line still has no level.
- **The CRN gap along railways is a clear, deliberate band.** CRN Chart 3 starts at 10 m, so AURIS gives no level nearer a track. Those contour nodes used to show as missing squares along the railway, and any of them switched the whole map back to Raw cells. The band within 10 m of each CRN railway is now drawn with an exact edge, like an emitting court, and the map key adds "No CRN level within 10 m". Interpolated and SmartSmooth presentation carry on everywhere else. Levels are unchanged.

## Bug fixes
- **Padel courts in the 3D view stay on their enclosure in Low, Medium and High.** The court surface and slab used the road-paint material, which widens distant paint by moving each vertex along its texture coordinates. On courts those coordinates are plan positions, so the playing surface slid several metres off the glass and mesh. Only Ultra, which renders the true geometry, drew it in place. Court lines still widen with distance, now about their own centre lines.

## New features
- **Contours never contradict a receptor.** SmartSmooth's Simplify and Smoothing may move a contour line within its level tolerance, but never across a receptor in the contour plane. A receptor is always drawn in the band its level is in, at every slider setting. Before, at strong settings a line could pass beside a receptor on the wrong side. For example, P1930's REC_001 (66.96 dB) was drawn in the 60–65 dB band at Simplify 100 %.

## Changes
- **Faster exact contours near buildings.** The lateral-path search's estimates now follow the same rule as the search: a path bends only where an object holds it. Near building corners the search no longer explores routes it would refuse. P1991 contours calculate in about 1 minute instead of 3½ minutes. Results are identical.
- **Faster start-up of each exact solve on built-up sites.** The obstacle-visibility table is built in a quarter of the time. On P2005 Unit A, exact receivers run twice as fast for small batches. Results are identical.
- **Faster area sources on sites without terrain.** Each area source's sections are calculated in one batch. P2001 is 18 % faster. Results are identical.
- **Switching from Raw to Interpolated or SmartSmooth refines in proportion to the model.** Reusing a calculated Raw grid made each receiver look almost free to calculate. Refinement then took its 20,000-point maximum, and the step-line search took on more than its time allowed. Both now budget by what the grid actually cost.

## Bug fixes
- **Step lines found before the time limit are kept.** When the search for verified steps in the contour field (drawn as lines rather than scallops) reached its 150 s limit, it discarded every line it had already proven. P2001 Aberdare lost all 12 lines on every Calculate. The lines proven by the limit are now drawn.

## New features
- **Receptor labels in 3D: names only, and one label per stack.** The Labels tile's arrow opens a short menu:
  - **Names and levels** or **Names only**.
  - **Stacks: one label with the range** (the default), for example "Flats 1-6 48.0–52.3 dB" above the top floor, or **Stacks: a label per floor**.

  The choice is saved with the 3D view.

## Changes
- **3D haze is a pale blue-grey, as real air is.** The horizon sky, and the haze that takes its colour, read teal. Ultra's haze is also a little greyer than the sky behind it, as aerosol haze is.
- **Smoother depth of field.** The live depth of field is worked at full resolution, so its blur no longer shows square steps.
- **Clean glass and court mesh in Ultra.** Ultra blends glass and mesh with what lies behind them, by their opacity, and light through them is dimmed by the share each pane lets through. Before, each sample either saw the glass or passed through it at random, so courts stayed blotchy while the image built up.

## Bug fixes
- **Lateral paths round buildings bend only where an object holds them (ISO 9613-2:2024, 7.4.3).** A path could double back at a corner with nothing inside the bend, for example at two points along a straight barrier, instead of going round the end of the terrace. On the P-projects 114 of 317 receptors change, by at most 0.24 dB (P2001 REC_003 +0.24 dB). P2001's receptors calculate in 8.6 s instead of 10.5 s.
- **Adjoining courts on level platforms are level.** Courts less than two aprons apart (P2001's are 0.94–0.99 m apart) each had their own level, so a court's apron climbed onto its neighbour and creased it: wavy in 3D, and cut along terrain triangles in the calculation. Adjoining courts now share one level, the area-weighted mean of their own. On P2001 with its courts levelled, receptor levels move by between −0.22 dB and +0.10 dB.

## New features
- **Contour accuracy: Exact or Draft.** Settings › Contours › Accuracy. Exact, the default, calculates every grid point exactly as a receptor, as before.

  Draft splits each area source by distance only, without the extra cuts along screening edges or the 1 mm terrain-following of the source surface. It is much faster on padel courts and walled yards, but approximate:
  - **On P2001** (five padel courts inside their own glass walls) the 2 m grid takes about a tenth of the time. Outside the courts, 95% of points are within 0.2 dB of Exact, and the largest difference is 0.8 dB.
  - **Elsewhere** it can be several dB out next to buildings: up to 3.6 dB on P1922, 3.4 dB on P2003 and 2.9 dB on P2005 Unit A.

  Receptor levels are always calculated exactly, whichever accuracy is chosen. Contours remember the accuracy they were calculated with.

## Changes
- **Faster exact calculations near many buildings and walls.** A lateral path around buildings needs a map of which building corners can see each other. Each path used to build its own map; each map is now taken from one map of the whole model. Results are identical to the last decimal place. P2001's exact 2 m grid takes 417 s instead of 531 s.
- **The steps after the contour grid share one set of workers.** The checks before refinement no longer solve their receivers one at a time (P2001: 18 s to 3 s).
- **Results: Receptor ID first.** The receptor table starts with a short ID (REC_004 reads 4), then the receptor's name, floor and assigned building. Exports keep the full model ID in its own column.

## Bug fixes
- **Renamed receptors and buildings show their new names in Results at once.** The table showed the names as they were when the levels were calculated, so a receptor renamed afterwards still read REC_004 and its building BLD_006. The scenario comparison already showed the new names.
- **A saved calculation lists receptors as the model now stacks and assigns them.** With an earlier run selected, floors added to a stack since then showed as separate, unassigned ground-floor receptors.
- **Receptor names and buildings sit level with their row.** Only names spanning several floors are aligned to the top.

## New features
- **Padel results follow ProPG Sport & Leisure.** Results › Padel now judges courts against the ANC/IOA/CIEH guide (draft, June 2026), Section 11:
  - **50 dB LAeq,1h outside**, from the courts alone;
  - **65 dB LAFmax outside** for the ball strikes, and 60 dB in a night period;
  - **the change in the existing ambient**, classed short-term with the guide's table (below 1 dB negligible, 1–3 minor, 3–5 moderate, 5 or more major).

  The verdict, the receptor table and the paragraph for the report say which criterion governs, by how much, and how the ambient changes. The inside LAFmax (45 dB) is now an optional extra criterion, off by default.
- **Survey data.** Results › Padel › Survey data… holds your measurement positions:
  - the ambient LAeq,1h in the hours of use, plus the first and last hours where they differ;
  - the background LA90;
  - the typical existing LAFmax.

  Each receptor is assigned the position that represents it; with one position, every receptor uses it. Each receptor's row then shows the change in ambient and its effect, and the court's LAFmax against the existing maxima (context, as §11.2 suggests).

## Changes

## New features
- **Internal levels from room details (BS 8233:2014 Annex G).** Results › Internal › Room details… calculates each room's internal level from its façade, using Equation (G.1) of the simplified method (after BS EN 12354-3): L2 = Lff + 10 lg(n·A0/S·10^(−Dn,e,w+Ctr/10) + Swi/S·10^(−Rw+Ctr,window/10) + Sew/S·10^(−Rw+Ctr,wall/10)) + 10 lg(S/A) + 3, with A0 = 10 m² and A = 0.16 V/T. You enter the room volume, reverberation time (0.5 s by default) or absorption area, façade and window areas, window and external wall Rw+Ctr, and the ventilators (trickle vents, through-wall vents, or none for mechanical ventilation) with their Dn,e,w+Ctr and count. Values can be set for each room type or for one selected receptor. There are three scenarios: windows partially open (15 dB from the façade level by default, editable; BS 8233 G.1 and WHO 1999), windows closed with trickle vents, and windows closed with mechanical ventilation. You state the basis of the external level: each receptor's sound field (Façade receptors are façade levels; Free field and Method convention receptors are taken as free field, the cautious reading), or free field or façade for every receptor. A façade level is taken as free field + 3 dB. Criteria are BS 8233 Table 4 (bedrooms 35 dB LAeq,16h by day and 30 dB LAeq,8h at night; living rooms 35 dB and dining rooms 40 dB by day). Max levels uses the same room reduction against the 45 dB LAFmax night guideline (WHO 1999; ProPG 2017; BS 8233 sets no LAFmax value). The live readout in the dialog shows each scenario's reduction while you edit.
- **Glazing and ventilation specification.** With room details on, Internal › Specification works out the window Rw+Ctr and vent Dn,e,w+Ctr that bring every receptor to its Table 4 criterion, and in bedrooms to 45 dB LAFmax at night when maximum levels have been calculated. It does this by inverting Equation (G.1). Glazing and vents can share the sound the wall leaves room for equally, or one can be held at its entered value while the other is solved. Each requirement is rounded up to the whole decibel. The schedule has one row per plot, storey, façade and room type (one per receptor outside buildings) and shows the external levels, the governing target, the required ratings and the scenario. Rows where partially open windows already meet the target say so. Copy specification for Word pastes it as a Word table, with tab-separated text for spreadsheets. Export specification to Excel… saves it with its basis notes.
- **Day at GF, night at first floor.** BS 4142, Internal and BS 5228 each have an option to assess a receptor stack's ground-floor receptor by day and its first-floor receptor at night, on one row (the Floor column reads "GF day · Fl. 1 night"). Upper floors keep their own rows, and receptors without both a ground and a first floor are unchanged. It is off by default and is saved per assessment. The BS 4142 Word table and the specification follow it.
- **Night event counts in Max levels.** Results › Max levels now counts, at each receptor, the night events above 45 dB LAFmax inside (through the Internal page's window) and above 60 dB LAFmax outside, and gives the 10th-highest LAFmax of the night. A count over the limit (more than 10 events, editable) is shown in red. The tooltips list the sources making the events. Both thresholds, the limit and the night period can be edited. The basis is WHO Guidelines for Community Noise (1999), 3.4 and Table 4.1 (45 dB LAFmax not more than 10–15 times a night), ProPG (2017) Stage 2 Element 2, and ProPG Stage 1 Figure 1 notes (more than 10 events above 60 dB LAFmax). This is guidance, not a standard. The columns are in Copy Table and Excel.
- **Event counts come from your inputs, never assumed.** A source whose night period is set to events counts those events. Any other source with a maximum takes the number of night events you give it under Max levels › Events per night, and its LAeq does not change. Until you give one, it is listed as "count not given" and the receptor's count shows as a lower bound (≥).
- **Transport pass-bys as your inputs.** Under Max levels › Transport pass-bys you can enter a train or HGV pass-by as a reference LAFmax at a distance, or as an SEL with its equivalent duration (LAFmax = SEL − 10 log10 τ). Give it a number of night pass-bys and the road, railway or line it is measured from. At each receptor its maximum follows the distance law you choose: 20 log10 for one vehicle or 10 log10 for a long train. The distance is from the nearest point of the centreline, in plan, with no screening. Every table, tooltip and statement labels these values as inputs you provided.
- **ProPG view in Results.** Results › ProPG gives each receptor's ProPG: Planning & Noise (2017) Stage 1 initial site noise risk for day (LAeq,16h) and night (LAeq,8h), on Figure 1's scale and the same edges as the Contours ProPG palettes. When there are more than 10 night events above 60 dB LAFmax, a negligible night risk becomes low (Figure 1 notes, marked ▴). The view also gives Stage 2 Element 2, BS 8233:2014 Table 4 (living room by day, bedroom at night, through the Internal page's window, with note 7's relaxation of up to 5 dB). Element 3 checks the receptors you mark as gardens or patios (right-click a row › External amenity area) against BS 8233:2014 7.7.3.2: 50 dB desirable, 55 dB upper guideline LAeq,T. Façade receptors can be converted to free field (−3 dB), which is off by default. A caution appears when the periods are not 16 h / 8 h, or when results are the CRTN LA10 index.
- **Acoustic Design Statement skeleton.** ProPG › Stage 2 and design statement… opens a window with fields for the site description, Element 1 (good acoustic design prompts), Element 4 (other relevant issues) and your recommendation to the decision maker. Beside them is an editable statement in ProPG's order, with the model's numbers filled in: Stage 1 table, Element 2 internal levels and night events, Element 3 amenity areas, and any pass-bys you entered. Copy for Word pastes it as rich text with tables. Your edits are saved with the project, and Update from model rebuilds the statement from the latest results.
- **Tonality evidence for BS 4142.** Results › BS 4142 › Tonality evidence… applies the one-third octave method of BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 (9.3.2, Annex C). A band's LZeq must exceed both neighbouring bands by at least 15 dB (25–125 Hz), 8 dB (160–400 Hz) or 5 dB (500 Hz–10 kHz). It runs on each receptor's predicted third-octave spectrum, propagated from entered third-octave source data with each band's parent-octave ISO 9613-2 attenuation (50 Hz–10 kHz). It also runs on a spectrum you type or paste, such as your own measurement, with optional residual band levels so masking is taken into account. Where it finds a tone, it suggests the 9.3.2 correction of +6 dB beside your tonality correction. AURIS never applies the correction: you set it. Octave-only and broadband sources are listed as not included, and no spectrum is inferred for them. The panel shows the latest result, and Copy for Word gives the evidence table with its limitations.
- **Uncertainty budget for BS 4142.** Results › BS 4142 › Uncertainty… combines three terms for each receptor by root-sum-square: the sound power uncertainty you enter, the ISO 9613-2:2024 Table 4 accuracy for its source paths and the background uncertainty you enter (BS 4142 Clause 10). It shows Lr − LA90 ± U (U = 1.96 σ, about 95 %) and says whether the Clause 11 initial estimate could change within ±U. Table 4 states no coverage, so you choose how its values are read: a 95 % half-width (the default) or one standard deviation. The choice is stated with the result. Paths outside Table 4 are flagged: beyond 1 km, above 200 m, or over terrain that is not approximately flat (the mean propagation height differs from the flat-ground value by 50 % or more, as in ISO 9613-2 D.5). For those paths U is a lower bound. With uncertainty entered, Copy table for Word adds ±U and "within ±U" columns. The report basis now carries an uncertainty paragraph.
- **Scheme assessment (DMRB LA 111).** Results › All scenarios › Scheme assessment (also under More) pairs your Do-Minimum and Do-Something scenarios for the opening and future years with a day and a night period, as LA 111 Revision 2 3.51 compares them. For each receptor it gives the short-term change (Table 3.54a: negligible below 1.0, minor 1.0–2.9, moderate 3.0–4.9, major 5.0 dB or more), the long-term change (Table 3.54b: below 3.0, 3.0–4.9, 5.0–9.9, 10.0 dB or more) and the non-project change. It compares the do-something level with LOAEL and SOAEL (Table 3.49.1: day 55/68 dB LA10,18hr façade, night 40/55 dB Lnight free field; editable under 3.50). It shows the Table 3.58 initial significance and the Table 3.60 circumstances that can be read from the levels, and gives the Table 3.55a/b counts for dwellings and other sensitive receptors. Every table copies for Word and exports to Excel. Levels are read from the saved runs and never changed.
- **Significance matrix and Noise Insulation Regulations screen.** The scheme assessment adds a sensitivity × magnitude significance column from DMRB LA 104 Table 3.8.1, with a sensitivity for each receptor. The matrix can be edited to match your project's own method. A Noise Insulation Regulations 1975 screen checks the 68 dB(A) L10,18h relevant level, the 1 dB(A) increase over the prevailing level and the 1 dB(A) effective contribution, taken from a scenario without the new or altered highway. It is a screen, not a determination of eligibility.

The starters are BS 4142 plant, CRTN residential, Padel courts and BS 5228 construction. Each sets up its periods: the BS 4142 7.2 reference intervals (1 h by day, 15 min at night, rated on their busiest interval), CRTN Day 07:00–23:00 and Night 23:00–07:00, or the BS 5228 ABC periods. It also sets receptor defaults and heights (BS 4142: 1.5 m by day, 4.0 m at night; CRTN: a 1.5 m / 4.0 m floor pair) and the operating hours new sources start with (padel 07:00–22:00; construction Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00, Sat 08:00–13:00). New contour sheets use SmartSmooth and a layout with client and consultant cards from your company profile. Templates set up structure only: no objects, maps or results. File › Save as Template… keeps the current project's setup, including these defaults, in your profile's templates folder.
- **Operating hours for each source.** Point, line and area sources and courts have operating hours: Always (the default, which matches earlier versions), a preset such as 07:00–19:00, or typed hours with optional days ("Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00; Sat 08:00–13:00", "22:00–02:00"). The share of each period inside the hours becomes an on-time, time-weighted. A period with clock times takes its operating hours over its length. A reference interval (1 h, 15 min, worst hour) takes its busiest interval inside its window. With days given, the busiest operating day decides. The hours are their own named correction ("Operating hours 07:00–19:00: 12 of 16 h, −1.2 dB") in the calculation trace and in Why this level?, before the on-time. A percentage on-time then applies while the source operates. Set the hours in the Inspector or in the Inputs table. Several selected sources are set in one undo step.
- **A receptor height for each period.** A receptor can have its own height in a period, for example 1.5 m by day and 4.0 m at a first-floor bedroom window at night. That period is calculated at that height. The Inspector shows a height per period (blank uses the receptor's height). Results add a Height column ("Day 1.5 m · Night 4.0 m") when any receptor has one, and each level's tooltip gives the height it was calculated at. Receptors without period heights are unchanged.
- **Inputs, edited like a spreadsheet.** Edit name, height, level, group, operating hours, X/Y of point objects and Calculate in place. A level can be edited when it is the input itself (broadband, manual, the same in every period). Cmd+D fills the first selected cell down the selection. Cmd+C copies cells. Cmd+V pastes a block copied from Excel over several rows. Each of these is one undo step, and cells that cannot take a value are named in place. Paste Receptors makes receptors from rows of name, X, Y and height, in local metres or OSGB easting/northing (recognised, or say Local/OSGB in a fifth column), as one undo step.
- **Typed placement in the Inspector.** A point source, receptor or ground point takes X and Y typed in model metres or, when the project is georeferenced, as OSGB E/N (Local | OSGB E/N switch). The switch is hidden when the project has no georeference.
- **Linked selection.** Selecting a receptor or any object in Results, Inputs, the 3D view or on a contour sheet selects it in the Editor, and selecting in the Editor highlights its row in Results and Inputs and the object in 3D. A workspace that is not on screen catches up when you open it, so selecting everything in a large model stays as quick as before.
- **Show in Editor.** Right-click a Results row and choose Show in Editor, or Command-click the row or a marker on a contour sheet: AURIS switches to the Editor, selects the object and brings it into view.
- **What changed since this result?** The out-of-date chip in the status bar (click its label), the Results banner and the Contours banner now open a list of the edits made since the result was calculated, grouped by kind: object, field, and old → new value, from the model saved with the run. Names, colours and labels are left out because they do not change a level. Each object has Reveal, and Recalculate affected brings the result up to date. The list is cached per result and edit (about 60 ms the first time on a 300-building model). For contours calculated in an earlier session, the comparison is with the latest receptor calculation, and the list says so.
- **Tools menu.** Every drawing tool is listed with its single-key shortcut (V Select, H Pan, P Point source, B Building, ⇧B Noise barrier and the rest).
- **Object menu.** Combine and Subtract buildings, Auto place receptors and Merge roads have moved here from Edit › Select.
- **Keyboard focus halo.** When you move focus with the keyboard, a soft teal glow shows around the focused button, segmented control, field or toolbar tile. It is a blur outside the control, not an outline, and it goes away at the next click.
- **Name the source in the band editor.** Frequency bands now open with the source's name at the top (for example "Honda EU10i generator" or a condenser's make and model). Apply renames the source, and a Notes field holds the measurement position and height, operating condition and meter. Notes are kept with the source and saved to My library whatever the quantity. Bands, quantity, name and notes are one undo step.
- **Bars and levels as one object.** Each band has a bar with its level directly beneath. Thirds are bracketed into octaves, with the octave's energetic sum shown once. A dot marks an octave with only some thirds entered, and bands outside the ISO 9613-2 range are muted. Hover a bar to see the entered, A-weighted and derived sound power levels, or click it to edit that band. Editing a level eases its bar to the new height (immediate under Reduce Motion).
- **Faster band entry.** ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ change a level by 1 dB (with ⇧, 0.1 dB). Right-click a band to clear it or its octave. In 1/1 octave, a quiet second row shows each band A-weighted, or as sound power when the bands are sound pressure.
- **Calibrate a source to a measurement.** For point and area sources (Inspector › Calibration, or Project › Calibrate Source to Measurement…), enter a measured LAeq or octave-band Leq at a receptor or a point. AURIS solves the sound power so the model reproduces the measurement through its own receptor calculation, with the project's ground, terrain, screening and reflections; it does not use a closed-form Lp → Lw conversion. This avoids counting the radiation factor Q and the ground reflection twice. For broadband levels the solve finds one value; for octave bands it finds one value per band. The dialog shows the solved sound power, the model's band response and the residual (within 0.1 dB; normally under 0.01 dB). Nothing changes until you choose Apply, which is one undo step. Per-period sound powers move by the same amount, and on-times are left alone. The source keeps the calibration record (position, measured values, period, date, method). The Inspector reports the calibration out of date when the buildings, barriers, ground, terrain, propagation settings, method, source geometry, measurement position or the sound power itself change, and Re-solve runs it again. AURIS warns when the measurement was closer than twice the source's largest dimension (ISO 9613-2 Clause 4, raster factor k = 0.5). Proposed mitigation is left out of the solve, because a measurement describes the site as it is.
- **Field edit state.** A field you are typing in shows a soft amber outline as soon as its value differs from the saved one. Press Enter or click away and the outline eases to teal, then fades after about a second; Escape puts the saved value back. A value the field cannot take shows red. Values the app fills in itself never show amber. Applies to every text and number field, and is instant with Reduce Motion.
- **Stepping with modifier keys.** Every − / + key, spin-box arrow and the Up/Down keys in those fields step by 1 with a click, by 5 with Shift and by 0.1 with ⌘. Whole-number fields such as Bands step by 1 with ⌘. Fields that step in other units (5 % opacity, 0.1 m heights) scale the same way. Limits and decimals are kept, and the tooltip shows the steps.
- **Delete, Select All and clipboard keys in other workspaces.** When the macOS menu bar handles these keys outside the Editor, they now go to the table or view you are in. Delete in a Results or Inputs table can no longer remove plan objects you cannot see.
- **Side panel scroll position.** Pressing Enter in a field, or clicking away from it, no longer scrolls the Inspector (objects and Project) to another place. The field you committed stays where it was, even when rows above it appear or disappear. The Contours sheet panel, 3D side panel and Settings behave the same way.

## New features
- **Low frequency (NANR45) on the Internal tab.** When the model has third-octave source data, Results › Internal shows a quiet "Low frequency (NANR45)" card; Assess opens it. It compares a receptor's internal one-third-octave Leq from 10 Hz to 160 Hz with the NANR45 criterion curve (Defra, Revision 1, December 2011, Table 2), with the 5 dB relaxations for noise that occurs only during the day (Section 4.1) and for steady noise (Section 4.2). A band exceeds the curve when its internal level is above it; the card gives the margin in every band, the worst band and a plain-English summary, and notes that a sound up to about 5 dB below the curve may still be audible (Section 4.2).
- **Internal levels from a window reduction.** Internal = external − reduction: 13 dB in every band by default (a partially open window), editable for the project or one receptor, or entered per band from test data.
- **Measured levels for complaint investigations.** Levels can be predicted, or measured inside or outside: type or paste a row of third-octave Leq into the table (blank bands are not assessed). Measured exceedances in the 50 Hz band or from 80 Hz to 160 Hz carry the Section 4.2 notes on fridges and traffic.
- **Charts and tables for reports.** Copy chart puts a 300 dpi chart on white (receptor, period, assumptions footnote, exceedances in red with their margin) on the clipboard for Word; Save chart writes PNG, SVG or PDF; Copy table pastes as a Word table. Settings are saved with the project, and every change is an undo step.
- **Assessment readiness.** The report basis and Results now list what the assessments still need, apart from whether the calculation is within the validated software scope. The list covers missing BS 4142 backgrounds or BS 5228 ambients for an assessed period, and BS 4142 outcomes within 3 dB of a category boundary while broadband sources use the 500 Hz estimate. It also flags receptors with sources more than 1 km away, which is beyond ISO 9613-2 Table 4. Mixed sound-field bases within one assessment are flagged, as are bases the standard does not expect (BS 4142 free field; BS 5228 ABC façade). So are BS 8233 criteria compared with periods other than 16 h by day or 8 h at night, CRTN night levels that equal the day because only the 18-hour flow is entered, and roads with traffic but 0 % heavy vehicles. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Copy table for Word (BS 4142).** Results › BS 4142 copies the assessment in report layout: receptor, period with its reference interval, specific sound level LAeq,Tr, each character correction, rating level LAr,Tr, background LA90,T, the excess of the rating over the background, sound field and the Clause 11 initial estimate. It pastes into Word as a real table, and into a spreadsheet as tab-separated text.
- **Exclude from assessment.** Right-click a receptor in Results to exclude it from assessment, for example a measurement position. It is still calculated and listed, but it is left out of the summaries, counts, readiness and the Word table, and named in a note below the table. Undo reverts it.
- **Sound-field conversion, by choice.** BS 4142 can assess Façade receptors at their level less 3 dB, and BS 5228 can assess Free field receptors at their level plus 3 dB. Both are off by default. Assessment tables now show each receptor's sound field.
- **Draw, then edit.** When you place or finish an object, it is selected and the side panel switches to the Inspector. Esc cancels a shape you are drawing, and a second Esc returns to Select.
- **Assessment inputs in Undo.** BS 4142 backgrounds, corrections and background basis, pasted or typed values for single receptors, Internal (BS 8233), maximum-level and BS 5228 inputs are now named undo steps. Typing a value is one step.

## Changes
- **BS 4142 outcomes in the standard's words.** Initial estimates read "Indication of a significant adverse impact", "Indication of an adverse impact" or "Indication of a low impact", each "depending on the context" in exports. A rating above the background by less than 5 dB is no longer labelled "Low to adverse": it reads "Above background, below +5 dB". Outcomes are classified on the difference as shown (0.1 dB), so +4.96 dB shows as +5.0 dB and is classed at +5.0 dB. The basis sheet states this rounding rule.
- **BS 5228 ABC as Table E.1 reads.** The ambient is rounded to the nearest 5 dB once, for every category. Above the C value, an effect is significant only when the site raises the total by more than 3 dB, so exactly +3.0 dB is not significant. Site levels are judged as shown.
- **Corrected citations.** BS 4142 character corrections are cited as the subjective method (9.2). The 45 dB LAFmax night guideline is attributed to WHO (1999) and ProPG (2017), not BS 8233.
- **"Within validated software scope".** The report basis status no longer says "Ready for client-facing reporting". The status describes the software scope only, and the separate Assessment readiness list covers the assessment.
- **The metric is named everywhere.** Results column headers, the Excel and clipboard headers, the assessment columns and basis sheets show the metric and clock times, for example "LAeq,16h 07:00–23:00". CRTN on the Q18 basis shows "LA10,18h 06:00–24:00". The sheet title block and the default legend heading show the metric too, and the summary line no longer reads "· dB".
- **Copy Table copies what you see.** Only the columns on screen are copied. Excel exports still include every column.
- **One way to say "out of date".** The status chip, the Results and Contours banners, the inspector, Inputs and the 3D façade panel all say results are out of date because the model has changed, and they all offer **Recalculate** ("Recalculate all" for several results). The Results banner has its own Recalculate button. The validated-scope line is hidden while results are out of date.
- **Clearer CRTN night and heavy-vehicle inputs.** The TRL (2006) conversion option now says it uses TRL Method 3 for night. The road inspector notes when the night level follows the 18-hour flow (so night equals day) and when heavy vehicles are 0 % on a road with traffic. Defaults and calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Sound field label.** "Existing convention" now reads "Method convention".
- **Third-octave levels below 50 Hz are labelled as an extension.** ISO 9613-2 gives attenuation from the 63 Hz octave. In the NANR45 card each third-octave band from 50 Hz to 160 Hz takes its parent octave's attenuation; 10 Hz to 40 Hz use the 63 Hz octave's terms (divergence, ground, screening and the rest) with no atmospheric absorption. This is stated in the card, the calculation trace and the chart footnote, together with NANR45's own caution (Section 1.1) that it is not a prediction method. Calculated receptor levels and contours are unchanged.

## Changes
- **The sheet key shows the glyphs on the map.** A receptor or point source with its own glyph (or a receptor with its own colour) gets its own row in the Objects key, drawn with that glyph and named after its objects ("Measurement Position"; "MP" for MP1, MP2), instead of a generic row with the default glyph.
- **CRTN roads with light traffic.** A road below CRTN's 1,000 vehicles per 18 hours (50 an hour) is now calculated instead of stopping the run: CRTN's flow line is extended and the low-flow correction is held at the edge of its chart, which errs on the high side. CRTN asks for a measurement at such flows, so the calculation names those roads and calls their levels indicative, and the road inspector says so under the flow. To keep a road for the drawing only, untick **Include in calculations** in its inspector.
- **Buildings read as solid forms at midday.** A high sun now leaves shaded walls a soft blue-grey against white sunlit faces, with gentle occlusion where walls meet the ground and in corners, and the sky is brighter on the sun's side so walls facing away from it separate. Mornings, afternoons and sunsets keep their look.
- **One look on every quality level.** Low, Medium, High and Ultra now share the same colours; what changes from level to level is the lighting detail: Low draws no cast shadows and light occlusion, Medium adds soft shadows and occlusion, High adds sharper contact shadows, reflections and bounce light, and Ultra is path traced.

- **A calmer, more compact 3D toolbar.** 11 controls instead of 21, so the time scrubber fits even in a 1440-pixel window. One Frame tile (selection, or everything), one Façades tile for choosing buildings and calculating, projection and display styles in menus, a bullseye for noise contours and a tag for labels. Quality is a named pill (Low, Medium, High, Ultra) that rolls to the new name instead of signal bars, with each level explained in its menu and on keys 1–4.
- **Done, in place.** Copy, Save and Render confirm with a tick on the Render tile itself.
- **Tidier side panel and popovers.** The side panel drops its duplicate title, camera and badge rows, hides layers 3D cannot draw yet and shows 'Show all objects' only while something is isolated; the inspector names the object type and shows sound power to one decimal. Round lines is a separate switch, and Advanced keeps separate Simplify and Smoothing. Older sheets open at the nearest Smoothness.

## New features
- **A rebuilt 3D view.** The 3D view has a new look, new lighting, exact ground and noise results drawn with the legend's own colours, and it keeps up with a 120 Hz display.

Projects that never chose a date use midsummer, so Midday puts the sun high in the south.
- **Studio lighting.** A key light and sky, plus optional fill and rim lights, each with direction, height, strength and colour. Four arrangements are built in (Clay, Soft overcast, Dramatic, Elevation), and you can save your own presets; they are kept on this Mac for every project.
- **Noise results in 3D from the Contours tab.** Noise contours in 3D now use the Contours tab's palette, bands, gradient and isolines directly, so there is nothing to set up twice. Colours match the legend exactly, and band edges and isolines stay sharp however close you zoom. A **Results** button in the 3D toolbar switches between the current result and saved runs, and turns noise contours, isolines, a horizontal noise slab and façades on and off separately.
- **Noise slab.** A translucent noise map at the height of a calculated grid, shown in 3D at its real height.
- **Storey façade maps.** Façade results can be shown per storey: each storey of each façade bay takes the colour of the highest level calculated on it, like an elevation drawing. Each building has a ground-floor and typical floor height (with optional exact floor heights); cells above the limit are hatched and the legend counts them; each building's most exposed and quietest façades are marked; hovering a cell shows its storey, direction, level and margin to the limit.

## Changes
- **The 3D look matches the Ultra render on every quality level.** Low, Medium, High and Ultra share one grade. In the afternoon it is the Ultra clay look: soft periwinkle shadows, near-white sunlit walls with a warm touch, soft blue occlusion where buildings meet the ground, warm light bounced from the ground onto shaded walls, and haze that fades the distance. Low draws no cast shadows, for a clean basic view.
- **Smooth shadows.** Shadows no longer show stripes or stair-steps at any distance or sun height, on Medium, High and Ultra, and buildings have soft contact shadows at their base.
- **120 Hz in 3D.** The 3D view now draws in step with the display, up to 120 Hz, and High and Ultra fit a 120 Hz frame while moving: dropped frames while orbiting fell from 10–18% to about 0.2%, also on a 1,000-building model.
- **Animations at the display's rate.** Panels, popovers, menus, the splash, progress bars and the 3D toolbar now animate at the screen's refresh rate (120 Hz on a 120 Hz display) instead of 60 Hz.
- **A new 3D toolbar.** The 3D toolbar uses the same buttons as the Editor's. Icons show the current setting (the sun's place for the time of day, bars for the quality level), the selection glides between Select, Orbit and Pan, popovers unfold from their button, and Render shimmers while it works. **Reduce Motion** is respected.
- **Editing in 3D is immediate.** Changing one object now updates only that object: on P2003 a building drag step takes 15 ms instead of 491 ms, a contour style change 36 ms instead of 504 ms, and the basemap switch 157 ms instead of 1.1 s. The 3D view opens about three times faster.
- **The 3D ground is the calculated ground.** The ground in 3D is built from the same triangles and heights the noise calculation uses (no difference inside the survey on the projects tested); it shades smoothly while slopes, banks and kerbs stay sharp, and roads and railways are no longer drawn sunk into it.
- **Sharp drawings close up in 3D.** Basemap drawings are redrawn at screen resolution near the camera, PDF drawings from their original vectors, so thin lines and text stay crisp instead of blurring or stepping.
- **Smoother editing on large models.** The plan keeps what it has drawn and repaints only what changes: on a 1,000-building model, moving the pointer over the plan takes about 2–8 ms a frame instead of 50 ms, wheel zoom 5 ms instead of 12 ms (the zoomed view sharpens a moment after the wheel stops), and the first frame of a pan, drag or rubber band 13 ms instead of 27–56 ms. Panning keeps antialiased lines throughout. What is on screen at rest, and every export, is drawn exactly as before.
- **Contour calculations on large models fit in memory.** Each calculation worker holds its own copy of the model, so a 1,000-building site with roads needed over 8 GB with a worker per core, enough to make a 16 GB Mac swap. Contour and receptor calculations now start only as many workers as the free memory holds for that model; small projects are unaffected.
- **Multiply and screen contour blends in 3D keep sharp results.** Over a basemap, multiply and screen blends now draw from the calculated levels (sharp at any zoom) instead of a pre-painted picture. Multiply matches the 2D blend to about 3 ΔE on a light drawing; the other blends still use the painted picture.
- **Crisper terrain contours.** Terrain contour lines are now drawn by the 3D renderer from the ground's own height: the same thin width on screen near and far, fading out with distance and where lines would crowd together, and in Ultra renders too.
- **Berms shown as terrain shade like the ground.** Their slopes are smooth and their crest and toe stay sharp, as on the surrounding ground.
- **Plainer 3D labels.** Toolbar, layer and status wording now matches the rest of the app: Noise contours, Noise isolines, Terrain contours, Results, Façades, storeys.
- **Receivers keep their colour.** Receptor and source markers are the same colour on every quality level and at every time of day.
